sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得一个月的所有新闻访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不会想错过。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: I want to tell you about a new show from Serial Productions and the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我想向你介绍来自 Serial Productions 和《纽约时报》的一档新节目。

sentences.en: It's called The Trojan Horse Affair, and it's hosted by Brian Reed of S-Town and a doctor-turned journalist named Hamza Syed.
sentences.zh: 它叫《特洛伊木马事件》，由 S-Town 的布赖恩·里德和一位弃医从文的记者哈姆扎·赛义德共同主持。

sentences.en: It's a mystery that began when a strange letter appeared laying out a supposed plot by Islamic extremists to infiltrate schools in Birmingham,
sentences.zh: 这是一个谜团，始于一封奇怪的信件的出现，信中阐述了伊斯兰极端分子渗透伯明翰学校的所谓阴谋，

sentences.en: England.
sentences.zh: 英格兰。

sentences.en: This letter set off a national panic, led to multiple investigations, and to lifetime bans from the British education system.
sentences.zh: 这封信引发了全国性的恐慌，导致了多项调查，并终身禁止进入英国教育系统。

sentences.en: But no one could answer a simple question, who wrote the letter?
sentences.zh: 但没有人能回答一个简单的问题：是谁写了这封信？

sentences.en: That's what Brian and Hamza tried to figure out.
sentences.zh: 这就是布赖恩和哈姆扎试图弄清楚的事情。

sentences.en: Take a listen to the first episode, and if you want to hear the entire series, search for The Trojan Horse Affair wherever you listen to podcasts.
sentences.zh: 听听第一集吧，如果你想听完整系列，可以在任何你听播客的地方搜索《特洛伊木马事件》。

sentences.en: And thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: This is my first story as a journaliSt. I hadn't planned for it to be my last story, but it probably will be, given what's happened in the years I've been working on this.
sentences.zh: 这是我作为记者的第一个故事。我原本没打算让它成为我的最后一个故事，但鉴于我从事这项工作这几年所发生的事情，它很可能就是了。

sentences.en: It's about a letter that surfaced in my city and had huge consequences for Britain.
sentences.zh: 它关于一封出现在我所在的城市并对英国产生巨大影响的信件。

sentences.en: This letter launched four government investigations, changed our national policy, and ended careers.
sentences.zh: 这封信引发了四项政府调查，改变了我们的国家政策，并断送了许多人的职业生涯。

sentences.en: It's hurt some of the country's most vulnerable children.
sentences.zh: 它伤害了该国一些最脆弱的儿童。

sentences.en: A letter that many people who've seen it agree is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 许多看过这封信的人都认为它荒谬绝伦。

sentences.en: It's unsigned, undated.
sentences.zh: 它没有署名，也没有日期。

sentences.en: Didn't it look like a serious document, didn't it?
sentences.zh: 它看起来一点也不像一份严肃的文件，不是吗？

sentences.en: It just seemed comical.
sentences.zh: 它简直显得滑稽可笑。

sentences.en: I think, what the hell is this?
sentences.zh: 我想，这到底是什么鬼东西？

sentences.en: I remember looking at it for some time, thinking, what on earth is this?
sentences.zh: 我记得盯着它看了好一会儿，心想，这到底是什么东西？

sentences.en: The infamous letter, was it written on parchment, in blood?
sentences.zh: 那封声名狼藉的信，是用羊皮纸写的，还是用血写的？

sentences.en: So you're presenting me with a document that turned our lives upside down?
sentences.zh: 所以你拿给我看了一份把我们的生活搅得天翻地覆的文件？

sentences.en: I first learned at the letter in 2014.
sentences.zh: 我第一次听说这封信是在2014年。

sentences.en: I wasn't a journalist then.
sentences.zh: 我那时还不是记者。

sentences.en: I was a doctor who'd quit medicine, living in Birmingham, England, making my breakfast at 1pm, listening to the news,
sentences.zh: 我是一个放弃了医学事业的医生，住在英格兰伯明翰，下午1点钟在做早餐，听着新闻，

sentences.en: when I heard about the discovery of a secret communique between Muslim extremists.
sentences.zh: 这时我听说发现了穆斯林极端分子之间的秘密密谋。

sentences.en: They were discussing a plot to infiltrate our city schools and run them on strict Islamic principles, potentially with the aim of radicalising students.
sentences.zh: 他们在讨论一个渗透我们城市学校并以严格的伊斯兰原则管理它们的阴谋，潜在目标可能是将学生激进化。

sentences.en: Someone had forwarded the letter anonymously to the local government, the Burma City Council, but it was missing the first and last page.
sentences.zh: 有人将这封信匿名转发给了当地政府伯明翰市议会，但它缺少了第一页和最后一页。

sentences.en: So it was unknown exactly who wrote it or who they were sending it to.
sentences.zh: 因此，确切是谁写的或他们是发给谁的，都不得而知。

sentences.en: According to the intercepted pages, the plot had a codename, Operation Trojan Horse.
sentences.zh: 根据截获的页面显示，这个阴谋有一个代号：特洛伊木马行动。

sentences.en: I have to admit, when this story about Muslims in Birmingham first broke, as a Muslim in Birmingham, I was alarmed.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，当这个关于伯明翰穆斯林的故事首次爆发时，作为伯明翰的一名穆斯林，我感到很惊慌。

sentences.en: It sounded possible.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实有可能。

sentences.en: Kids across Britain, across Europe, were flying off to Syria to join this group called ISIS.
sentences.zh: 英国各地、欧洲各地的孩子们都在飞往叙利亚加入这个叫 ISIS 的组织。

sentences.en: And Birmingham has been home to quite a few terrorists.
sentences.zh: 而且伯明翰一直是不少恐怖分子的发源地。

sentences.en: My neighbour was a terroriSt. The guy who killed five people and then tried to run into parliament with a knife.
sentences.zh: 我的邻居就是一个恐怖分子。那个杀死五个人然后试图拿着刀冲进议会的人。

sentences.en: He did his planning in a flat above the Persian restaurant across the street from me.
sentences.zh: 他的策划地点就在我街对面波斯餐厅楼上的公寓里。

sentences.en: So I wasn't surprised watching, as over the next several months,
sentences.zh: 所以，当接下来的几个月里发生的事情展开时，我一点也不感到惊讶，

sentences.en: Operation Trojan Horse snowballed into a huge national story.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊木马行动如滚雪球般演变成一个巨大的全国性新闻。

sentences.en: A number of schools in Birmingham have been infiltrated by hardline MusliMs. Headlines like
sentences.zh: 伯明翰的一批学校被强硬派穆斯林渗透。诸如此类的头条新闻

sentences.en: Islamist plot, jihadist plot, alleging a conspiracy by all...
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰阴谋、圣战阴谋，声称所有人都在密谋……

sentences.en: And the government responded with full force.
sentences.zh: 政府做出了全力回应。

sentences.en: The Prime Minister got involved, convening his cabinet to discuss the threat.
sentences.zh: 首相介入了，召集他的内阁讨论这一威胁。

sentences.en: The national government sent in a bunch of investigators, including Scotland Yard's former head of counter-terrorism,
sentences.zh: 国家政府派出了大批调查人员，其中包括苏格兰场前反恐负责人，

sentences.en: to look into two dozen schools in majority Muslim areas of Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 对伯明翰穆斯林占多数地区的二十多所学校进行了调查。

sentences.en: Like I say, it was all very frightening.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这一切都非常吓人。

sentences.en: Until a few months later, when the various investigators finally started reporting their findings.
sentences.zh: 直到几个月后，各调查组终于开始汇报他们的调查结果。

sentences.en: They'd found no plot called Operation Trojan Horse.
sentences.zh: 他们没有发现任何名为特洛伊木马行动的阴谋。

sentences.en: They'd seen no signs that anyone had been radicalised, no evidence of violence or planned violence.
sentences.zh: 他们没有看到任何人被激进化的迹象，也没有暴力或计划暴力的证据。

sentences.en: They didn't bring any terror charges against anyone working at the schools they'd looked into.
sentences.zh: 他们没有对他们所调查的学校中的任何人提出任何恐怖主义指控。

sentences.en: But despite all of that, despite finding no plot, investigators still concluded that something terrible was happening in
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，尽管没有发现任何阴谋，调查人员仍然得出结论认为，有可怕的事情正在发生

sentences.en: Birmingham schools.
sentences.zh: 伯明翰的学校。

sentences.en: The letter helped them uncover that Muslims had influenced the schools in a dangerous way.
sentences.zh: 这封信帮助他们发现穆斯林以危险的方式对学校产生了影响。

sentences.en: Government officials snapped into action.
sentences.zh: 政府官员迅速采取行动。

sentences.en: Things that should not have happened in our schools were allowed to happen.
sentences.zh: 本不该在我们的学校发生的事情却被允许发生了。

sentences.en: Our children were exposed to things they should not have been exposed to.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子接触到了他们本不该接触的事物。

sentences.en: The fallout has been huge.
sentences.zh: 余波是巨大的。

sentences.en: Prime Minister David Cameron, as we said, is calling a special meeting of the government's extremism task force.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，首相大卫·卡梅伦正在召开政府极端主义特别工作组的特别会议。

sentences.en: Officials removed educators, revamped schools and renamed them.
sentences.zh: 官员们撤换了教育工作者，改组了学校并重新命名了它们。

sentences.en: They mandated all schools in the country start teaching what they termed British values to make kids less susceptible to extremist ideas.
sentences.zh: 他们强制要求全国所有学校开始教授他们所谓的英国价值观，以使孩子们不易受到极端主义思想的影响。

sentences.en: They beefed up Britain's counter-extremism laws by making public sector workers like teachers and doctors part of the state's surveillance apparatus to now inform on their
sentences.zh: 他们加强了英国的反极端主义法律，让教师和医生等公共部门工作人员成为国家监控机构的一部分，现在向他们举报

sentences.en: co-workers and students and patients.
sentences.zh: 同事、学生和病人。

sentences.en: Today, if you stop someone on the streets of Britain and ask them what happened in Birmingham schools in 2014, if they follow the news they'll likely tell you that a
sentences.zh: 今天，如果你在英国街头拦住某人，问他们2014年伯明翰学校发生了什么，如果他们关注新闻，他们可能会告诉你

sentences.en: bunch of Muslims were up to no good.
sentences.zh: 一帮穆斯林在搞鬼。

sentences.en: There is another version of this story though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这个故事还有另一个版本。

sentences.en: It's one less told and far less popular.
sentences.zh: 这是一个较少为人所知、也远没有那么流行的版本。

sentences.en: That version of the Trojan horse affair is that nothing happened.
sentences.zh: 关于“特洛伊木马”事件的那个版本是，什么都没有发生过。

sentences.en: That these bearded brown educators were set up and the nation fell for it.
sentences.zh: 那些蓄着胡须、皮肤棕色的教育工作者遭人陷害，而全国上当受骗。

sentences.en: But it's always seemed to me that there's a simple way to figure out what really happened here.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，总觉得有一种简单的方法能弄清楚这里到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: The letter.
sentences.zh: 那封信。

sentences.en: Even with all the government inquiries, no authority, none of the investigators ever figured out who wrote it.
sentences.zh: 尽管进行了所有的政府调查，但没有任何权威机构、没有一个调查人员弄清楚是谁写的。

sentences.en: Remarkably, none of them even tried.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，他们当中甚至没有人尝试过。

sentences.en: And that, to me, seemed like a pretty glaring oversight.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是一个相当明显的疏忽。

sentences.en: The reason the country was looking at these schools with suspicion, the reason they were investigating them at all, was because this dodgy
sentences.zh: 这个国家之所以用怀疑的眼光看待这些学校，之所以对它们进行调查，是因为这封可疑的

sentences.en: letter showed up portraying the people who worked there as nefarious plotters, claiming they were sneaking Islam into schools like a Trojan horse.
sentences.zh: 信件出现了，它把在那里工作的人描绘成邪恶的阴谋家，声称他们像特洛伊木马一样把伊斯兰教悄悄引入学校。

sentences.en: The letter is what put the idea in authorities' heads.
sentences.zh: 这封信正是让当局产生这种想法的根源。

sentences.en: So I didn't see how you could know what Operation Trojan horse was or wasn't unless you got to the bottom of the Trojan horse letter.
sentences.zh: 所以我不明白，除非你追查到底弄清这封特洛伊木马信的真相，否则你怎么能知道“特洛伊木马”行动究竟是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Who wrote it and why?
sentences.zh: 是谁写的，为了什么？

sentences.en: A few years later, I decided to go to school for investigative journalism.
sentences.zh: 几年后，我决定去学习调查性新闻专业。

sentences.en: But my professor wasn't completely sold on a story I wanted to report from a student project, Operation Trojan horse.
sentences.zh: 但我的教授对我想作为学生项目报道的一个故事——“特洛伊木马”行动——并不是完全买账。

sentences.en: This was investigative journalism.
sentences.zh: 这可是调查性新闻。

sentences.en: He wanted me to unearth something new, not rake over some years-old story.
sentences.zh: 他希望我能挖掘出一些新的东西，而不是去重提几年前的陈旧故事。

sentences.en: As a doctor though, I'm familiar with the concept of a second opinion.
sentences.zh: 不过作为一名医生，我对“第二意见”的概念并不陌生。

sentences.en: So the night before my master's was set to start,
sentences.zh: 就在我的硕士课程开学的前一晚，

sentences.en: I went looking for one.
sentences.zh: 我去找了一个。

sentences.en: A doctor came to see me for a second opinion.
sentences.zh: 有个医生来找我看第二次意见。

sentences.en: One night in fall 2017,
sentences.zh: 2017年秋天的一个晚上，

sentences.en: I'm in a theater in Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 我在伯明翰的一个剧院里。

sentences.en: After my podcast, S-Town, came out, I went around doing some Q&As.
sentences.zh: 我的播客《S城》播出后，我到处去做问答交流。

sentences.en: Afterwards, people will sometimes come backstage to chat.
sentences.zh: 事后，人们有时会到后台来聊天。

sentences.en: And so this guy comes in, introduces himself as Hamza Syed.
sentences.zh: 于是这家伙进来了，自我介绍说叫哈姆za·赛义德。

sentences.en: He said he was changing careers to become a reporter.
sentences.zh: 他说他正在转行当记者。

sentences.en: He was beginning a master's program in investigative journalism the next day, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他第二天就要开始读调查新闻的硕士项目了。

sentences.en: And he wanted some advice.
sentences.zh: 他想征求一些建议。

sentences.en: He was speaking fast, like I might walk away at any moment.
sentences.zh: 他语速很快，好像我随时都会走开似的。

sentences.en: To be fair, I was told that I had five minutes with
sentences.zh: 说实话，有人告诉我，我和

sentences.en: Brian Reid, after which I'd be squirted out the building.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩·里德只有五分钟时间，之后我就会被轰出大楼。

sentences.en: I did not know that.
sentences.zh: 我当时不知道这一点。

sentences.en: Anyway, Hamza ran through the Trojan horse story for me, elevator pitch style.
sentences.zh: 总之，哈姆扎用电梯推销的风格，把“特洛伊木马”的故事给我过了一遍。

sentences.en: I'd never heard of it, but a guy I was with backstage, a producer I know from the BBC, he had.
sentences.zh: 我以前没听说过，但我和后台的一个人，一个我认识的BBC制作人，他听说过。

sentences.en: And he jumped in as Hamza was talking.
sentences.zh: 就在哈姆扎说话的时候，他插话了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, Trojan horse, he said.
sentences.zh: “对，对，特洛伊木马，”他说。

sentences.en: That was a big thing a while ago.
sentences.zh: 那在不久前曾是一件大事。

sentences.en: Some bad stuff went down.
sentences.zh: 发生了一些糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Muslim educators have been up to no good.
sentences.zh: 穆斯林教育工作者一直在搞鬼。

sentences.en: But it was cleared up.
sentences.zh: 但事情已经澄清了。

sentences.en: Old story.
sentences.zh: 老黄历了。

sentences.en: There was something
sentences.zh: 不过，哈姆za说过一件事

sentences.en: Hamza said, though, which afterwards I couldn't get out of my head.
sentences.zh: 我事后怎么也挥之不去。

sentences.en: He kept talking about a letter which had set off this whole cascade of consequences, whose origins were still a mystery.
sentences.zh: 他一直谈论一封信，这封信引发了一连串的后果，而其根源至今仍是个谜。

sentences.en: So when I got home to New York, I read the letter.
sentences.zh: 所以当我回到纽约的家时，我读了这封信。

sentences.en: It looked like a caricature of a missive between two terrorists, filled with Islamophobic tropes about conniving and scheming MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像是两名恐怖分子之间信件的滑稽模仿，充满了关于穆斯林暗中勾结和阴谋的伊斯兰恐惧症老生常谈。

sentences.en: It's missing pages.
sentences.zh: 它缺页了。

sentences.en: Parts of it are too dark to read, like it got jammed in the Xerox machine.
sentences.zh: 有些部分太黑了看不清，就像卡在复印机里了一样。

sentences.en: It instructs the recipient to destroy it after reading.
sentences.zh: 它指示收件人在阅读后将其销毁。

sentences.en: It struck me as a funky document for a government to take seriously, especially because from what I read, the government hadn't even looked into who wrote the letter or why.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，政府把这样一份奇怪的文件当回事很不可思议，尤其是据我所知，政府甚至没有去调查是谁写的这封信，也没有调查原因。

sentences.en: There was a strange lack of curiosity about this instigating document.
sentences.zh: 对于这份煽动性的文件，人们出奇地缺乏好奇心。

sentences.en: I thought to myself, it seems like somebody should try to figure out who wrote that thing.
sentences.zh: 我心想，似乎应该有人设法弄清楚是谁写那东西的。

sentences.en: And then I thought, well, wait, this journalism student's doing that.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，等等，这个新闻系学生正在做这件事。

sentences.en: Maybe I had to give him a hand.
sentences.zh: 也许我得帮他一把。

sentences.en: And here we are, years later, at the end of a dizzying, farcical, and enraging investigation
sentences.zh: 就这样，多年后的今天，在经历了一场令人眼花缭乱、荒诞不经且令人愤怒的调查之后

sentences.en: in which one mystery led to another, led to another, tracing this letter's path of destruction across multiple continents.
sentences.zh: 在这场调查中，一个谜团引出另一个谜团，再引出另一个谜团，追溯这封信在各大洲的破坏轨迹。

sentences.en: In defiance of many unhappy officials and some aggressive attempts to shut our reporting down.
sentences.zh: 不顾许多不高兴的官员以及一些阻止我们报道的粗暴尝试。

sentences.en: From Serial Productions and the New York Times, I'm Brian Reed.
sentences.zh: 来自连环制作公司和纽约时报，我是布莱恩·里德。

sentences.en: I'm Hamza
sentences.zh: 我是哈姆za

sentences.en: Said.
sentences.zh: 赛义德。

sentences.en: Presenting to you the most elaborate student project ever.
sentences.zh: 向您呈现史上最精心策划的学生项目。

sentences.en: This is the Trojan Horse Affair.
sentences.zh: 这就是“特洛伊木马事件”。

sentences.en: I got the call from Brian while I was in class.
sentences.zh: 我上课时接到了布莱恩的电话。

sentences.en: My phone started ringing from a New York number.
sentences.zh: 我的手机开始响，是一个纽约的号码。

sentences.en: I asked my professor if I could take it.
sentences.zh: 我问教授我能不能接。

sentences.en: He said no.
sentences.zh: 他说不行。

sentences.en: I asked if I could go use the toilet.
sentences.zh: 我问我能不能去上个厕所。

sentences.en: He said yes.
sentences.zh: 他说可以。

sentences.en: I answered.
sentences.zh: 我接了。

sentences.en: And Brian told me he wanted in on my investigation, but that I would need a producer.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩告诉我他想加入我的调查，但我需要一个制作人。

sentences.en: I said yeah, sure, all casual.
sentences.zh: 我很随意地说了句好吧。

sentences.en: I had no idea what a producer did.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道制作人是干什么的。

sentences.en: Soon, he started getting in touch with missions for me to complete.
sentences.zh: 很快，他开始联系我，给我布置任务。

sentences.en: First one.
sentences.zh: 第一个。

sentences.en: He'd secured a recorder for me in Birmingham and said there's something I had to do.
sentences.zh: 他在伯明翰给我弄到了一台录音机，并说我有一项任务必须去完成。

sentences.en: It was supposed to be a basic bread and butter assignment.
sentences.zh: 这本来应该是一项基础的常规任务。

sentences.en: Go record a meeting.
sentences.zh: 去录下一场会议。

sentences.en: Hamza had seen an event advertised called Trojan Horse The Facts, where some of the educators who'd been accused of carrying out the plot would be speaking publicly.
sentences.zh: 哈姆扎看到了一则名为“特洛伊木马真相”的活动广告，广告称一些被指控实施该阴谋的教育工作者将公开讲话。

sentences.en: They insisted the
sentences.zh: 他们坚称

sentences.en: Trojan Horse Affair was just an Islamophobic stitch-up.
sentences.zh: “特洛伊木马事件”只是一场蓄意陷害的伊斯兰恐惧症闹剧。

sentences.en: The event hashtag was Trojan Hoax, and they were trying to clear their names.
sentences.zh: 活动的话题标签是“特洛伊骗局”，他们正试图洗清罪名。

sentences.en: They'd never gotten their lives back on track after the story died down.
sentences.zh: 在事件热度平息后，他们的生活再也没有回到正轨。

sentences.en: They'd lost their jobs and been made into pariahs by the national media.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了工作，被全国主流媒体视作社会弃儿。

sentences.en: But afterwards,
sentences.zh: 但事后，

sentences.en: Hamza calls me and says when he showed up at the spot, a community center at 5 p.m., the receptionist told him,
sentences.zh: 哈姆扎打电话给我，说当他下午5点赶到那个地方——一个社区中心时，前台接待员告诉他：

sentences.en: It's been canceled.
sentences.zh: 活动取消了。

sentences.en: The event's been canceled.
sentences.zh: 活动已经取消了。

sentences.en: Did they give you any, well, wait, did they give you any other information?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有给你提供，呃，等等，他们有没有给你提供任何其他信息？

sentences.en: Like, what did they, like...
sentences.zh: 比如，他们说了什么，或者...

sentences.en: No, they just said it's been canceled, and that was it.
sentences.zh: 没有，他们只说取消了，就这样。

sentences.en: I said, no, this is, you know, I felt like an idiot, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，这，你知道的，老实说我当时觉得自己像个傻子。

sentences.en: This can't be a good omen, I thought, to mess up your first journalism assignment.
sentences.zh: 我想，这可不是什么好兆头，竟然把你的第一项新闻任务搞砸了。

sentences.en: But then, more people started showing up, confused, like me, until a man in one of those safety vests swings around the corner, tells us to follow him, and takes us up the street
sentences.zh: 但随后，更多的人开始出现，和我一样一头雾水，直到一个穿着那种安全背心的男人转过街角，让我们跟着他，把我们带到了街上

sentences.en: to a wedding hall, where everyone was gathering instead.
sentences.zh: 去了一个婚礼大厅，大家转而都在那里聚集。

sentences.en: It's a lot of people, maybe over 100.
sentences.zh: 人非常多，大概有一百多名。

sentences.en: And as I explained to Brian, while I'm setting up the microphone...
sentences.zh: 正如我向布莱恩解释的那样，当时我正在设置麦克风……

sentences.en: And it turned out that the original venue had received phone calls from the national newspaper, specifically this guy, Nick Timothy.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，原本的场地接到了来自全国性报纸的电话，具体来说是这个人，尼克·蒂莫西。

sentences.en: He's like a reporter or a publisher, or what is he?
sentences.zh: 他是个记者还是出版商，还是说他到底是什么人？

sentences.en: He's a columnist, I think, for The Telegraph.
sentences.zh: 我想他是《每日电讯报》的专栏作家。

sentences.en: And not just any old columniSt. Nick Timothy used to be the chief of staff to the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 而且可不是什么普通的专栏作家。尼克·蒂莫西曾担任过首相的幕僚长。

sentences.en: He was essentially Theresa May's right-hand man.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是特蕾莎·梅的得力助手。

sentences.en: I spoke to the guy who ran the community center, who told me,
sentences.zh: 我跟社区中心的负责人谈过，他告诉我，

sentences.en: Nick Timothy had actually emailed, not called.
sentences.zh: 尼克·蒂莫西其实是发了电子邮件，而不是打电话。

sentences.en: He wouldn't let me see the email, but according to others at the meeting, the implication was, if you hold this event, I will associate you with extremists in the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 他不肯让我看那封邮件，但据会上的其他人说，其暗示的意思是，如果你们举办这个活动，我就会在报纸上把你们和极端分子联系起来。

sentences.en: And that worked.
sentences.zh: 这一招奏效了。

sentences.en: The community center pulled the plug, and Nick Timothy published a triumphant column, which I'd missed because I was on YouTube all day, watching instructional videos on how to use
sentences.zh: 社区中心取消了活动，尼克·蒂莫西发表了一篇得意洋洋的专栏文章——我因为整天都在YouTube上看关于如何使用

sentences.en: my recorder, in which he confirmed his paper had gotten the event cancelled, and wrote that the
sentences.zh: 我的录音机的教学视频而错过了这篇文章——他在文中证实他的报纸让这次活动被取消了，并写道，

sentences.en: proposed meeting was, quote, a shocking attempt to deny the Trojan horse scandal, and, quote,
sentences.zh: 拟议中的会议是“对否认‘特洛伊木马’丑闻的一次令人震惊的尝试”，并且“

sentences.en: the people behind the Trojan horse are trying to do it all over again, and right under our noses.
sentences.zh: ‘特洛伊木马’事件的幕后黑手正试图卷土重来，而且就在我们的眼皮底下。”

sentences.en: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Trojan horse, or hoax, the discussion and debate.
sentences.zh: 各位女士先生，大家晚上好，欢迎来到“特洛伊木马：是真是假”讨论与辩论会。

sentences.en: So here they were, the teachers and school volunteers, allegedly behind Operation Trojan horse,
sentences.zh: 所以他们就在这里，那些据称是“特洛伊木马行动”幕后黑手的教师和学校志愿者，

sentences.en: along with their defenders, academics and activists, and an educational barrister and a union leader, packed in this wedding hall instead.
sentences.zh: 还有他们的辩护人、学者、活动人士，以及一名教育大律师和一名工会领袖，挤在这个婚礼大厅里。

sentences.en: I am really, really concerned that simply holding a public, open meeting like this becomes controversial.
sentences.zh: 我非常非常担心，仅仅举办这样一场公开的、开放的会议，就会引发争议。

sentences.en: Just the fact we are holding this meeting seems to be an act of resistance right now.
sentences.zh: 光是我们正在开会这件事，现在看起来就成了一种抵抗的行为。

sentences.en: The people at this meeting called for an inquiry to correct the record on the Trojan horse affair.
sentences.zh: 参加这次会议的人呼吁展开调查，以澄清“特洛伊木马”事件的真相。

sentences.en: They believed the government had set them up.
sentences.zh: 他们认为政府陷害了他们。

sentences.en: So the fact that a former chief of staff to the prime minister, Nick Timothy, went out of his way to attack a grassroots event at a community centre,
sentences.zh: 因此，时任首相的前办公厅主任尼克·蒂莫西竟然专门跑去攻击一个社区中心的基层活动，

sentences.en: years after the Trojan horse affair, it just reinforced their suspicion, and mine quite honestly, that there was something dodgy that authorities were still keen to hide.
sentences.zh: 在“特洛伊木马”事件发生多年之后，这更加强了他们的怀疑——老实说，也加强了我的怀疑——即当局仍有一些不可告人的猫腻急于掩盖。

sentences.en: And then it was like a witch hunt.
sentences.zh: 然后这就像是一场猎巫行动。

sentences.en: Heads were rolling this way and that way.
sentences.zh: 一个个职位纷纷落马。

sentences.en: Hamza sent me the recording of the meeting.
sentences.zh: 哈姆扎把会议的录音发给了我。

sentences.en: I listened to it and I was interested to hear that one of the people who got on stage and spoke
sentences.zh: 我听了录音，很好奇地听到其中一位上台发言的人

sentences.en: was the man named repeatedly in the Trojan horse letter as the mastermind of Operation Trojan horse, the plot's alleged ringleader, a long-time school volunteer named Tahir Alam.
sentences.zh: 就是在“特洛伊木马”信件中被反复点名、被称为“特洛伊木马行动”幕后主使、该阴谋的所谓首领、长期担任学校志愿者的塔希尔·阿拉姆。

sentences.en: I've never been a danger to anyone.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有对任何人构成过危险。

sentences.en: I've never hurt anyone.
sentences.zh: 我从未伤害过任何人。

sentences.en: I've never had any police case against me or anything of the kind.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有吃过官司或诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I wasn't running a plot.
sentences.zh: 我根本没有策划什么阴谋。

sentences.en: You know, we are very proud of what we did.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们为我们所做的事感到非常骄傲。

sentences.en: I do not regret nor apologize for anything that I've done.
sentences.zh: 我对我所做的一切既不后悔，也不道歉。

sentences.en: There was nothing clandestine, hidden, or sinister about what we were doing.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的事情没有任何秘密、隐蔽或险恶之处。

sentences.en: We were very open and very transparent.
sentences.zh: 我们一直都非常公开、非常透明。

sentences.en: So when I landed in Birmingham to begin reporting, that's who we decided to go to first, Tahir Alam.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我抵达伯明翰开始做报道时，这就是我们决定首先去找的人，塔希尔·阿拉姆。

sentences.en: We figured, we're looking to find the source of this mysterious letter.
sentences.zh: 我们想，既然我们要寻找这封神秘信件的源头，

sentences.en: Might as well start with the guy it outed as an extremist plotter.
sentences.zh: 不如就从这个被信件指名为极端主义策划者的人开始查起。

sentences.en: Is this about to be the first radio interview you've ever done?
sentences.zh: 这会是你接受的第一次电台采访吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I need to be schooled beforehand, man.
sentences.zh: 我得提前接受点指导，老兄。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 什么意思？

sentences.en: Like, how so?
sentences.zh: 比如，怎么说呢？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, if this was me flying solo, I'd be like, well, whatever, I'll just do it in my style, you know?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，如果是我自己单干的话，我会觉得，管他呢，我就按自己的风格来，你知道吧？

sentences.en: But this is, this is, you know...
sentences.zh: 但这个，这个嘛……

sentences.en: And what is your style?
sentences.zh: 那你的风格是什么？

sentences.en: Do you have a style?
sentences.zh: 你有什么风格吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm a lot...
sentences.zh: 我觉得我比……

sentences.en: How many of these have you done?
sentences.zh: 你做过多少次这种采访？

sentences.en: None.
sentences.zh: 一次也没有。

sentences.en: But I have an idea in my head of what my style could be.
sentences.zh: 但我脑子里对我的风格应该是什么样有个概念。

sentences.en: I think you're a lot more sensitive than I am, put it that way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你比我敏感得多，这么说吧。

sentences.en: Do you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: I mean, like, you're...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比如，你是……

sentences.en: I'm the more sensitive one.
sentences.zh: 我是比较敏感的那一个。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Don't you think so?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know you that well.
sentences.zh: 我和你没那么熟。

sentences.en: I wonder what we're wearing.
sentences.zh: 我在想我们穿着什么。

sentences.en: Salaam, darling.
sentences.zh: 萨拉姆，亲爱的。

sentences.en: Salaam.
sentences.zh: 萨拉姆。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Ill-fitting button-down shirt.
sentences.zh: 一件不太合身的衬衫。

sentences.en: Khakis.
sentences.zh: 卡其裤。

sentences.en: Welcome.
sentences.zh: 欢迎。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We're going to be in that room there.
sentences.zh: 我们要去那边的房间。

sentences.en: This room?
sentences.zh: 这个房间吗？

sentences.en: We kick off our shoes.
sentences.zh: 我们脱下鞋子。

sentences.en: He shows us to a room at the front of his place.
sentences.zh: 他带我们去他住所前方的房间。

sentences.en: Sorry, you have to sit on slightly uncomfortable chairs there.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，你们得坐在那些稍微不太舒服的椅子上。

sentences.en: Hamz and I squeeze behind two school desks, meant for children.
sentences.zh: 哈姆兹和我挤在两张为儿童准备的课桌后面。

sentences.en: There are protractors lying around.
sentences.zh: 周围散落着量角器。

sentences.en: A whiteboard with sketches of geometric shapes.
sentences.zh: 一块画着几何图形草图的白板。

sentences.en: A creative writing workbook titled Descriptasaurus.
sentences.zh: 一本名为《描述恐龙》的创意写作练习册。

sentences.en: Tahir has converted this room from his garage into a tiny makeshift classroom, where it appears he tutors students quietly.
sentences.zh: 塔希尔把这个房间从他的车库改造建成了一个简陋的小教室，看起来他平时在这里安静地辅导学生。

sentences.en: Because one result of the Trojan horse letter is that the government has banned him from ever volunteering or working officially in schools again.
sentences.zh: 因为“特洛伊木马”信件事件产生的一个后果是，政府禁止他再次在学校担任志愿者或进行任何官方工作。

sentences.en: Tahir is in front of us in his office chair.
sentences.zh: 塔希尔坐在我们面前的办公椅上。

sentences.en: Confident, erudite, framed by his bookshelf, filled with texts about Islam and British history.
sentences.zh: 自信、博学，背景是他的书架，上面摆满了关于伊斯兰教和英国历史的书籍。

sentences.en: I pull a copy of the letter out of my backpack.
sentences.zh: 我从背包里掏出一份信件的复印件。

sentences.en: You know, it's a completely anonymous letter, undated, claiming that there is a plot to take over and Islamize the schools in Birmingham, led by Tahir Alam, which is myself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一封完全匿名的信，没有日期，声称伯明翰的学校存在一个由我——塔希尔·阿拉姆领导的接管和伊斯兰化计划。

sentences.en: But I speak from a vantage point where I actually know the truth.
sentences.zh: 但我说话的角度是我实际上知道真相。

sentences.en: I know the reality.
sentences.zh: 我了解现实。

sentences.en: Tahir denies being an extremiSt.
sentences.zh: 塔希尔否认自己是极端分子。

sentences.en: He denies engineering a plot.
sentences.zh: 他否认策划了一场阴谋。

sentences.en: He says the reality is that rather than corrupting schools as a radical conspirator, he, a first-generation immigrant from a poor Pakistani family,
sentences.zh: 他说，现实情况是，作为一个来自贫困巴基斯坦家庭的第一代移民，他没有像激进阴谋家那样腐蚀学校，

sentences.en: was responsible for one of the most miraculous school turnarounds in British education.
sentences.zh: 而是促成了英国教育史上最不可思议的学校大翻盘之一。

sentences.en: Until, he says, the letter arrived and destroyed him.
sentences.zh: 直到，他说，那封信到来并毁了他。

sentences.en: The story of this turnaround, it's not a secret.
sentences.zh: 这场彻底翻盘的故事，其实并不是什么秘密。

sentences.en: It's one Tahir shared with journalists before.
sentences.zh: 塔希尔以前就曾向记者分享过。

sentences.en: Not that it's done him much good in terms of clearing his name.
sentences.zh: 尽管这对他洗清罪名并没有什么实质性的帮助。

sentences.en: But this backstory does explain why the Trojan horse letter was so persuasive.
sentences.zh: 但这段背景故事确实解释了为什么那封“特洛伊木马”信件会如此具有说服力。

sentences.en: Because, Tahir told us, some of what was in that letter was true.
sentences.zh: 因为塔希尔告诉我们，信中的某些内容确实是真的。

sentences.en: Tahir begins his story one night in 1993, when he's watching TV and a show caught his attention.
sentences.zh: 塔希尔的故事要从1993年的一晚说起，当时他正在看电视，一个节目吸引了他的注意。

sentences.en: I just happened to be just lying on the sofa, really, and the programme came on.
sentences.zh: 我其实当时就只是躺在沙发上，然后节目就开始了。

sentences.en: It was a documentary, part of the BBC series, Panorama.
sentences.zh: 那是一部纪录片，是BBC《广角镜》系列节目的一部分。

sentences.en: Nine times out of ten, I would switch to something else.
sentences.zh: 十有八九，我都会换台看别的。

sentences.en: But I was just sitting there and I started watching.
sentences.zh: 但我当时就坐在那儿，开始看了起来。

sentences.en: Britain's new underclass is Asian and it's Muslim.
sentences.zh: 英国的新底层阶级是亚洲人，而且是穆斯林。

sentences.en: A once tightly knit community is now in crisis, with drug abuse, crime and family breakdown on the increase.
sentences.zh: 这个曾经紧密团结的社群如今陷入危机，吸毒、犯罪和家庭破裂现象不断增加。

sentences.en: And the title of this documentary was Underclass in Purda.
sentences.zh: 这部纪录片的标题是《面纱下的底层》。

sentences.en: In tonight's panorama, we investigate an Underclass in Purda.
sentences.zh: 在今晚的《广角镜》中，我们调查了《面纱下的底层》。

sentences.en: Purda meaning, you know, cover.
sentences.zh: 面纱的意思，你知道的，就是遮挡。

sentences.en: Meaning a veil, if you like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，意思是面罩。

sentences.en: Underclass in the veil, yeah.
sentences.zh: 面纱下的底层，是的。

sentences.en: In tonight's programme, we lift the veil on this new Underclass.
sentences.zh: 在今晚的节目中，我们揭开了这个新底层阶级的面纱。

sentences.en: A report from the...
sentences.zh: 这是一份来自……

sentences.en: The documentary opens with shots of brown men skulking around dark, cobblestone streets in a Muslim neighbourhood, in what the correspondent calls the Muslim ghetto.
sentences.zh: 纪录片的开场镜头是棕色皮肤的男子在穆斯林社区黑暗的鹅卵石街道上鬼鬼祟祟地游荡，这里被记者称为穆斯林贫民窟。

sentences.en: At night, it doubles as the local red light district.
sentences.zh: 到了晚上，这里兼作当地的红灯区。

sentences.en: It's a seedy world of vice and illicit drug dealing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满罪恶和非法毒品交易的肮脏世界。

sentences.en: Lurking in the shadows is a new Manningham phenomenon, the Pakistani pimp.
sentences.zh: 潜伏在阴影中的是曼宁厄姆的一种新现象，巴基斯坦皮条客。

sentences.en: He's like a regular pimp, but in a kurtha.
sentences.zh: 他就像普通的皮条客，只是穿着库尔塔长衫。

sentences.en: Part of the documentary takes place in Tahir's neighbourhood in Birmingham, called Alamrak, on the east side of the city.
sentences.zh: 纪录片的一部分拍摄地点在伯明翰塔希尔的社区，名叫阿拉姆拉克，位于该市的东部。

sentences.en: It's one of the poorest areas in England, and is majority Pakistani and Muslim.
sentences.zh: 这是英格兰最贫困的地区之一，居民大多是巴基斯坦人和穆斯林。

sentences.en: If you're not from Birmingham, and you're not brown, you may have heard that Alamrak is a great place to find a terroriSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是来自伯明翰，而且不是棕色皮肤，你可能听说过阿拉姆拉克是找恐怖分子的好地方。

sentences.en: If you're not from Birmingham and you are brown, you'll have heard Alamrak is a great place to find a wedding dress.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是来自伯明翰，而且你是棕色皮肤，你会听说阿拉姆拉克是买婚纱的好地方。

sentences.en: Admittedly, this BBC documentary is racist in a 90s TV kind of way, but it had a big impact on Tahir, because amidst the awkward brown gazing, some truly sobering facts emerge.
sentences.zh: 诚然，这部BBC纪录片带有90年代电视那种老式的种族主义色彩，但它对塔希尔产生了巨大的影响，因为在那些令人尴尬的猎奇目光中，浮现出了一些真正令人清醒的事实。

sentences.en: The presenter reports that Pakistani Muslims are incarcerated at disproportionately high rates.
sentences.zh: 主持人报道称，巴基斯坦裔穆斯林的监禁率高得离谱。

sentences.en: She says they have some of the highest rates of joblessness.
sentences.zh: 她说他们的失业率居高不下。

sentences.en: They're suffering from devastating health issues, terrible housing, domestic violence, with one underlying cause of it all, a lack of education.
sentences.zh: 他们正遭受着毁灭性的健康问题、糟糕的住房、家庭暴力的折磨，而这一切的根本原因只有一个，那就是缺乏教育。

sentences.en: This is the number I found most shocking.
sentences.zh: 这是让我觉得最震惊的数据。

sentences.en: About 20% of white students were leaving school without any qualifications, meaning they failed to pass the exams that would essentially be the equivalent
sentences.zh: 大约20%的白人学生离开学校时没有任何文凭，这意味着他们未能通过基本上相当于美国高中毕业证的考试。

sentences.en: of a high school diploma in the US.
sentences.zh: 相当于美国的高中毕业证。

sentences.en: And that rate, 20%, was roughly the same for most people of colour as well.
sentences.zh: 而这个20%的比率，对于大多数有色人种来说也大致相同。

sentences.en: But for Pakistanis and Bangladeshis,
sentences.zh: 但对于巴基斯坦人和孟加拉国人来说，

sentences.en: an astonishing 50% hold no qualifications whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 惊人的50%没有任何学历。

sentences.en: Half of us were basically failing school.
sentences.zh: 我们当中有一半人基本上都快要跟不上学校的进度了。

sentences.en: That hit the hair hard.
sentences.zh: 这给塔希尔带来了沉重的打击。

sentences.en: That the extent of education failure was so bad that we were at risk of creating an underclass of Muslims who were basically uneducated, prone to crime and unemployment.
sentences.zh: 教育失败的程度如此严重，以至于我们面临着这样一种风险：即培养出一个基本上没有受过教育、容易犯罪和失业的穆斯林底层阶级。

sentences.en: So I kind of sat there, and it made me feel guilty, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就坐在那儿，实际上这让我感到很内疚。

sentences.en: Guilt because I was one of the few people who made it from my family, one of the first ones to make it into university and to have a good job and so on.
sentences.zh: 内疚是因为我是家族中为数不多出人头地的人之一，是第一批考入大学并找到好工作的人之一。

sentences.en: But there was also a sense of humiliation, really, because I was from this community.
sentences.zh: 但实际上也有一种屈辱感，因为我来自这个社区。

sentences.en: The Harris family brought him to England in the 70s, when lots of people from Kashmir were moving here, largely because the British designed this huge dam
sentences.zh: 哈里斯家族在20世纪70年代把他带到了英国，当时许多克什米尔人搬到这里，主要原因是英国人修建了这座巨大的水坝，

sentences.en: that flooded swaths of land and displaced tens of thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 它淹没了大片土地，导致数万人流离失所。

sentences.en: And one solution the Brits got behind was to invite displaced Pakistanis over to England so they could improve the British economy by working in British factories and mills,
sentences.zh: 英国人想出的解决方法之一就是邀请流离失所的巴基斯坦人来到英国，这样他们就可以通过在英国工厂和作坊工作来改善英国经济，

sentences.en: which is what the Harris dad did.
sentences.zh: 哈里斯的父亲就是这么做的。

sentences.en: The Harris arrived in England as a nine-year-old who didn't speak any English and wouldn't become fluent for several years.
sentences.zh: 哈里斯九岁时来到英国，当时他不会说一句英语，好几年后才说得流利。

sentences.en: I knew one word of English only, which was F-O-R-D.
sentences.zh: 我只知道一个英文单词，那就是F-O-R-D。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know X, Y, Z, but I know F-O-R-D, that's it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不知道X、Y、Z，但我知道F-O-R-D，就这样。

sentences.en: I can relate.
sentences.zh: 我感同身受。

sentences.en: I couldn't speak any English when I first came here.
sentences.zh: 我刚来这里时也不会说英语。

sentences.en: I couldn't even speak forward.
sentences.zh: 我甚至连“向前（forward）”都不会说。

sentences.en: I was just like mute.
sentences.zh: 我当时就像个哑巴。

sentences.en: Football, that's what I knew, football.
sentences.zh: 足球，那就是我所知道的，足球。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's how you arrived here.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你来到这里的方式。

sentences.en: And the first school, when I came here, we arrived in...
sentences.zh: 而我刚来这里时的第一所学校，我们到达了……

sentences.en: ...is growing up angry and alienated from white society.
sentences.zh: ……在愤怒和与白人社会的疏离中长大。

sentences.en: Now the hair watched, as a documentary captured the next generation.
sentences.zh: 现在，纪录片记录下了下一代人的成长，塔希尔在一旁看着。

sentences.en: Pakistani kids who were born in Britain, being educated in state schools, still struggling to read, not able to recall basic English words.
sentences.zh: 在英国出生的巴基斯坦孩子，在公立学校接受教育，依然在阅读上苦苦挣扎，无法记起基本的英语单词。

sentences.en: The camera caught us to a park in Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 镜头把我们带到了伯明翰的一个公园。

sentences.en: It looked at the hair like Ward End Park, which is right across from where he went to school, in Alam Rock.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像伯明翰阿拉姆罗克的沃德恩公园，也就是塔希尔上学的地方的正对面。

sentences.en: I recognised the park, because we used to go and play there.
sentences.zh: 我认出了这个公园，因为我们过去常去那里玩。

sentences.en: And then I saw some children, and I said, oh, that's our neighbour's children.
sentences.zh: 然后我看到了一些孩子，我说，哦，那是我们邻居的孩子。

sentences.en: I recognised the kids here, even though he was from a distance.
sentences.zh: 我认出了这里的孩子，尽管他是从远处看的。

sentences.en: But I recognised who the kids are.
sentences.zh: 但我认出了这些孩子是谁。

sentences.en: We filmed an encounter with two Asian lads in a park in a Muslim quarter of Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 我们在伯明翰一个穆斯林聚居区的公园里拍摄了一次与两个亚裔小伙子的相遇。

sentences.en: These Asian lads, we use Asian to mean South Asian, by the way, they're skipping school.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，这些亚裔小伙子——我们用亚裔来指代南亚裔——他们正在逃学。

sentences.en: And the hair knew which school they were skipping.
sentences.zh: 塔希尔知道他们逃的是哪所学校。

sentences.en: It was the one he'd gone to as a kid, right next to that park.
sentences.zh: 那是他小时候上过的学校，就在那个公园旁边。

sentences.en: Parkview School.
sentences.zh: 派克维尤学校。

sentences.en: Another majority Muslim school, with miserable academic results.
sentences.zh: 另一所穆斯林学生占多数的学校，学业成绩糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: It's a secondary school, ages 11 to 16.
sentences.zh: 这是一所中学，招收11到16岁的学生。

sentences.en: It was a school where Tahir had done well enough to make it to college, and then university, before getting a good job in telecommunications.
sentences.zh: 正是在这所学校里，塔希尔表现得足够好，得以进入大学预科，然后是大学，之后在电信行业找到了一份好工作。

sentences.en: The documentary made him realise how rare his success was, and how little he'd done with it.
sentences.zh: 这部纪录片让他意识到他的成功是多么罕见，以及他用它所做的事情是多么少。

sentences.en: So Tahir decided to do something.
sentences.zh: 于是塔希尔决定做点什么。

sentences.en: He started a tutoring programme for kids in the neighbourhood, but what he was really interested in was volunteering at his old school,
sentences.zh: 他为社区的孩子们发起了一个辅导项目，但他真正感兴趣的是在他的老学校派克维尤学校志愿担任校董会成员。

sentences.en: Parkview, on what's known as their governing body.
sentences.zh: 在英国，校董会负责监督学校的运营，就像公司的董事会一样。

sentences.en: In England, a governing body oversees how a school is run, like a corporate board does a company.
sentences.zh: 它有点像美国的学校董事会，只不过它是针对一所特定学校的。

sentences.en: It's sort of like a school board in the U.S., except it's specific to one school.
sentences.zh: 他们可以有很大的影响力。

sentences.en: They can have a lot of influence.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，

sentences.en: So anyway,
sentences.zh: 塔希尔说，有一天下午，两个他不认识的派克维尤学生的家长敲响了他的房门。

sentences.en: Tahir says, one afternoon, a couple of Parkview parents he didn't know knocked on his door.
sentences.zh: 我们听说你有兴趣成为一名校董，他们说。

sentences.en: We hear you're interested in becoming a governor, they said.
sentences.zh: 这就像他们读懂了他的心思一样。

sentences.en: It was like they'd read his mind.
sentences.zh: 虽然实际上，

sentences.en: Though actually,
sentences.zh: 塔希尔最近在一次婚礼上谈到过想当校董，而这些家长听到了这个消息。

sentences.en: Tahir had been talking about wanting to be a governor at a recent wedding, and these parents got wind of it.
sentences.zh: 阿拉姆罗克的家长们多年来一直心怀怨恨和沮丧，他们曾一次次试图让当局对糟糕的学校采取点行动。

sentences.en: Resentment and frustration had been festering for years among parents in Alum Rock, who'd been trying and trying to get the authorities to do something about the dismal schools.
sentences.zh: 敲塔希尔家门的这些家长加入了派克维尤校董会，试图做出改变，但他们英语说得并不流利，也没有上过大学。

sentences.en: These parents at Tahir's door had joined the Parkview governing body in an attempt to make a change, but they didn't speak fluent English and hadn't gone to university.
sentences.zh: 而塔希尔是一个有学位、仍住在社区的专业人士。

sentences.en: Tahir was a professional with a degree who still lived in the neighbourhood.
sentences.zh: 我们很乐意推选你，他们告诉他。

sentences.en: We'd love to propose you, they told him.
sentences.zh: 就这样，

sentences.en: And with that,
sentences.zh: 塔希尔发现自己参加了派克维尤学校的下一次校董会会议，不仅被投票选为成员，还被选为主席。

sentences.en: Tahir found himself at the next governing body meeting of Parkview School, being voted in not only as a member, but as the chair.
sentences.zh: 所以那就是我于1997年1月7日成为校董的时候。

sentences.en: So that's when I became a governor on the 7th of January, 1997.
sentences.zh: 你还记得日期吗？

sentences.en: Do you remember the date?
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，我将在那里待上18年。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I was to remain there for 18 years.
sentences.zh: 塔希尔刚开始的时候，

sentences.en: When Tahir started,
sentences.zh: 派克维尤是全国最差的中学之一。

sentences.en: Parkview was one of the worst secondary schools in the country.
sentences.zh: 只有4%的学生及格。

sentences.en: Only 4% of students were passing.
sentences.zh: 只有百分之四的学生及格。
国家学校视察局最近将该学校列入特别干预名单，这是最低的排名，基本上是一种紧急状态，

sentences.en: The National School Inspection Agency had recently placed the school into special measures, the lowest possible ranking, an emergency status, basically,
sentences.zh: 这意味着派克维尤面临着被关闭的危险。

sentences.en: meaning Parkview was in danger of being shut down.
sentences.zh: 学校操场上爆发了一场场群殴。

sentences.en: There were brawls breaking out in the schoolyard.
sentences.zh: 在参观大楼时，

sentences.en: On a tour of the building,
sentences.zh: 塔希尔看到遭到破坏的浴室里，隔间没有门锁，马桶没有马桶盖。

sentences.en: Tahir saw vandalized bathrooms with stalls missing locks and toilets missing seats.
sentences.zh: 但塔希尔真正关注的焦点是那些自满的老师和行政人员。

sentences.en: But where Tahir really trained his focus was on the complacent teachers and administrators.
sentences.zh: 我们最初只是开始表示，很明显，孩子们应该取得更高的成绩，这种成绩是不可接受的，而且学校

sentences.en: We initially just started by saying that obviously children should be achieving higher, that the achievement was not acceptable, and the fact that the school
sentences.zh: 应当为这种失败承担责任。

sentences.en: was to blame for the failure.
sentences.zh: 这一观点对塔希尔来说是显而易见的——阿拉姆罗克的孩子们和任何地方的孩子一样有能力——却遭到了巨大的阻力。

sentences.en: This statement, so obvious to Tahir that the kids in Alam Rock were as capable as kids anywhere, was met with massive resistance.
sentences.zh: 要让学校承认他们自己就是问题所在，是非常困难的。

sentences.en: It was very difficult getting the school to accept that they were the problem.
sentences.zh: 人们不想接受这一点，因为他们已经把责任归咎于社区大约二十年了。

sentences.en: People didn't want to accept that because they'd been blaming the community for maybe two decades.
sentences.zh: 他们对孩子的期望实在是太低了。

sentences.en: They had such a low expectation of children.
sentences.zh: 塔希尔很早就注意到的一件事是，这所拥有近90%巴基斯坦学生的学校只有一名全职的

sentences.en: One thing Tahir noticed early on was that the staff of this school with nearly 90% Pakistani students had only one full-time
sentences.zh: 巴基斯坦穆斯林教师。

sentences.en: Pakistani Muslim teacher.
sentences.zh: 于是塔希尔开始寻找更多的穆斯林教职员工和校董。

sentences.en: So Tahir began searching for more Muslim staff and governors.
sentences.zh: 他做演讲，举办研讨会。

sentences.en: He gave presentations, held workshops.
sentences.zh: 他成了东伯明翰各地活动中的常客，站在他的小桌子或摊位后面，大力宣传让人们参与到当地学校中来。

sentences.en: He became a fixture at events around East Birmingham, standing behind his little table or booth, evangelizing for people to get involved in their local schools.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它。

sentences.en: I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢和孩子们在一起，因为我觉得我能带来改变。

sentences.en: I loved it with the children because I felt that I could make a difference.
sentences.zh: 这是马兹·侯赛因，塔希尔雇用的

sentences.en: This is Maz Hussain, the first Muslim teacher
sentences.zh: 第一位穆斯林老师。

sentences.en: Tahir hired.
sentences.zh: 他教数学。

sentences.en: He taught math.
sentences.zh: 我可以用我的语言、我的背景、我对他们出身的理解来带来改变。

sentences.en: I could use my language, my background, my understanding of where they come from to make a difference.
sentences.zh: 我认识他们的家人。

sentences.en: I knew their families.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，马兹能指出他决定投身教育的具体时刻。

sentences.en: Maz can point to a specific moment, by the way, when he decided to go into teaching.
sentences.zh: 有一个全景纪录片节目。

sentences.en: There's a panorama program.
sentences.zh: 它叫做《面纱下的底层阶级》。

sentences.en: It's called an underclass in Pardah.
sentences.zh: 很有冲击力的一段。

sentences.en: Powerful segment.
sentences.zh: 马兹·侯赛因说，从一开始，他就遇到来自大多是白人教职员工的严重偏见。

sentences.en: Maz Hussain says from the very beginning, he encountered serious prejudices among the mostly white staff.
sentences.zh: 有一群孩子来找我说，看，学校里有这么一个老师。

sentences.en: I had a group of children come to me and they said, look, there's this one teacher in school.
sentences.zh: 他总是叫我们“巴基佬（packies）”。

sentences.en: He always calls us packies.
sentences.zh: 他叫我们“巴基佬”。

sentences.en: He's calling us packies.
sentences.zh: 他是用开玩笑的方式叫的，但我们觉得这很冒犯。

sentences.en: He's doing it in a jokey way, but we find it offensive.
sentences.zh: 他们不敢告诉别人，但他们告诉我，看，他在冲我们发飙。

sentences.en: They're not able to tell anyone else, but they're telling me that, look, he's sweating at us.
sentences.zh: 这在任何情况下都是一种侮辱，但由老师对巴基斯坦学生说出这样的话尤其令人震惊。

sentences.en: That's a slur in any context, but especially shocking for a teacher to say to Pakistani students.
sentences.zh: 马兹告诉他们，

sentences.en: Maz told them,
sentences.zh: 我认为最好的做法是，让你们的家长写信给学校。

sentences.en: I think the best thing to do, have your parents write the score.
sentences.zh: 他向他们详细介绍了这样做的程序，

sentences.en: He talked them through the procedure for doing that
sentences.zh: 因为家长们并不知道。

sentences.en: because the parents don't know.
sentences.zh: 他说，最终学校调查了这名老师的行为。

sentences.en: He says eventually the school looked into the teacher's behavior.
sentences.zh: 就在你调查的同时，他辞职了，并在教工休息室发表了他的临别演讲，他说，在这个学校里，应该由我们的文化占主导地位，而不是这些孩子。

sentences.en: And while you're investigating, he resigned and he gave his final leaving speech in the staff room and goes, it should be our culture dominant in this school, not the kids.
sentences.zh: 他最后以这样的话结束：西方是最棒的（the West is the best）。

sentences.en: And he finished off with the words, the West is the beSt.
sentences.zh: 所有老师都鼓掌了。

sentences.en: And all teachers clapped.
sentences.zh: 所有老师都鼓掌了。

sentences.en: All teachers clapped.
sentences.zh: 种族主义无处不在。

sentences.en: The racism was pervasive.
sentences.zh: 拉兹万·法拉兹，前校董兼数学老师，说在她的第一次校董会会议上，有人向他展示了一份学生通过学校的一个项目被安排实习的地点列表，

sentences.en: Razwan Faraz, a former governor and math teacher, says at one of his first governing body meetings, he was shown a list of places the students had been given work placements
sentences.zh: 通过学校的一个项目。

sentences.en: through a program at the school.
sentences.zh: 全都是餐馆、超市、服装店。
